building.local_amendments_note: No city amendment to the building code was found, but Chapter 6 of the Greensboro Code of Ordinances was not read on the page (Municode blocked). The search summary of Article II reads that the state code 'shall be in effect as modified by the building code council in the City of Greensboro', which points to the state council's amendments, not city ones. Under G.S. 143-138(e) (read on ncleg.gov) the State Building Code applies throughout the state and a local code is not effective until the Building Code Council approves it.

permit.exempt_list_quote: (c) No permit issued under Article 9 of Chapter 143 of the General Statutes is required for any construction, installation, repair, replacement, or alteration costing forty thousand dollars ($40,000) or less and performed in accordance with the current edition of the North Carolina State Building Code in any single-family residence, farm building, or commercial building unless the work involves any of the following: (1) The addition, repair, or replacement of load-bearing structures. However, no permit is required for replacement of windows, doors, exterior siding, or the pickets, railings, stair treads, and decking of porches and exterior decks that otherwise meet the requirements of this subsection. (2) The addition or change in the design of plumbing. However, no permit is required for replacements otherwise meeting the requirements of this subsection that do not change size or capacity. (3) The addition, replacement, or change in the design of heating, air-conditioning, or electrical wiring, devices, appliances, or equipment, other than like-kind replacement of electrical devices and lighting fixtures. (4) The use of materials not permitted by the North Carolina State Building Code. (5) The addition of roofing, excluding replacement. (6) Any changes to which the North Carolina Fire Code applies.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Greensboro job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the North Carolina rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Greensboro college halls, distribution centers, manufacturing plants and medical offices, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** North Carolina's plumbing rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and they apply in every city in the state. Greensboro's plan reviewers work from them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the City of Greensboro issues building permits in Greensboro. Under North Carolina law, work in a commercial building that costs $40,000 or less needs no permit unless it involves load-bearing structure, a change to the plumbing, heating, air conditioning or electrical systems, materials the building rules don't allow, new roofing or anything the fire rules cover. The list doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask the city's Development Services office (336-373-2155) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** North Carolina's rules call for separate men's and women's restrooms, with signs, once a space holds more than 25 people (30 for an office, 100 for a store). Where each side needs only one toilet, two single-user rooms open to anyone may be used instead, and a family restroom doesn't have to be marked for one sex. The rules in force don't provide for a shared all-gender room with several stalls, so ask the City of Greensboro's Development Services office before planning one. State law leaves the question of who may use a multi-stall restroom to the General Assembly: state agencies, cities, counties and school boards may not set their own rules.
page.confirm_office: the City of Greensboro's Development Services office
page.install_rule: Commercial permits in Greensboro come from the city's Development Services office. State-licensed contractors pulling certain Greensboro permits keep a $2,000 contractor's bond on file with the city. North Carolina requires a state general contractor license when the project is valued at $40,000 or more, so smaller partition jobs generally don't need one. Confirm with the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a project valued at $40,000 or more, the contractor needs a North Carolina general contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** North Carolina has no state law setting wages on public construction, so a required wage applies only on federally funded or assisted projects over $2,000. For a carpenter on building work in Guilford County that rate is $20.68 an hour plus $9.15 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6.75% in Greensboro: 4.75% state and 2% Guilford County.
page.buyers_extra: - **Colleges and universities:** one material and one hardware standard across many buildings, with heavy-duty hardware for restrooms that see crowds between classes.
